photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: The photo documents two Tlingit men in traditional dress standing before carved totem/mortuary poles and Chief Shakes House at Wrangell, Alaska—clearly Tlingit material culture and daily life.

photo.name: stereoscope photograph
photo.title: stereoscope photograph (black and white)
photo.reason: A documentary stereoscope photograph shows two men standing before carved Tlingit mortuary totem poles (whale crest and bear crest) at Fort Wrangell, Alaska, a genuine Tlingit site and cultural practice.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: The photo shows three Native women in Sitka, Alaska, weaving spruce root baskets while wearing traditional blankets and head coverings — a documentary scene of Tlingit daily craft life, consistent with the claimed ethnicity despite the museum's cautious "(Tlingit?)" label.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (black and white); photographic print
photo.reason: Documentary postcard photo of Tlingit people walking to a potlatch in Wrangell, Alaska, with a man in ceremonial regalia (chief's blanket/headdress) carrying items for the ceremony — a genuine depiction of Tlingit communal/ceremonial life.

photo.name: stereoscope photograph
photo.title: stereoscope photograph (black and white)
photo.reason: The stereoscope photograph shows a group of Native Alaskan people wrapped in blankets, one man wearing a fur hat and necklace, photographed outdoors in Sitka, Alaska—consistent with a documentary photo of Tlingit dress and daily life in their homeland.

jewelry.name: Amulet
jewelry.title: Amulet
jewelry.reason: This is a carved ivory amulet (likely a sea lion or walrus tusk) incised with Northwest Coast formline designs showing stylized creatures, consistent with Tlingit shamanic/ritual regalia worn as personal adornment or charm.

household.name: krok, Fiskkrok, fish-hook
household.title: krok, Fiskkrok, fish-hook
household.reason: This is a carved wooden halibut fishhook with a metal barb, bound with spruce-root lashing and decorated with carved mountain-goat figures — a classic Tlingit fishing implement documented as collected in Wrangell, Alaska by a known collector.

household.name: krok, hook
household.title: krok, hook
household.reason: This is a wooden halibut hook with bone barb, lashed with root/withe wrapping and cordage — a fishing tool type made and used by Northwest Coast peoples including the Tlingit; the museum's own record attributes it to Tlingit (Vancouver Island area, though geographically that's Kwakwaka'wakw/Nuu-chah-nulth territory, the object type and attribution stand as recorded).

household.name: Spoon
household.title: Ladle
household.reason: A horn ladle with a carved wooden handle depicting a face and ring motifs, consistent with Northwest Coast (Tlingit) feast utensils used for serving food at ceremonial gatherings.

household.name: comb
household.title: comb
household.reason: The image shows a carved wooden comb with a crest-figure top, attributed to the Tlingit as a measuring-worm crest design, consistent with Tlingit-made household items.

household.name: Canoe model
household.title: Canoe Model
household.reason: A painted wooden model canoe with Northwest Coast formline design (ovoid eyes, stylized creature forms) consistent with Tlingit maritime craft and artistic tradition.

household.name: smoking-pipe
household.title: smoking-pipe
household.reason: The image shows a carved wooden pipe-bowl in the form of a human head with brass rims, inscribed "Sitka" (a Tlingit town in Alaska); this is a well-documented type of Tlingit-made carved wood pipe, consistent with the museum's attribution.

household.name: fish-hook; figure
household.title: fish-hook; figure
household.reason: The image shows a carved wooden halibut hook shank in the form of a bird-shaman figure wearing a conical hat and frog-cape motif, a well-documented Tlingit/Northwest Coast fishing implement, matching the museum's attribution ("probably" Tlingit) with plausible cultural design elements.

household.name: Hook
household.title: Halibut Hook
household.reason: This is a carved wood Tlingit halibut hook with plant fiber lashings and bone/metal point, a traditional fishing tool made and used by the Tlingit — though it is wood and fiber, not metal, so "metalwork" is the wrong category.

instruments.name: Rattle
instruments.title: Rattle
instruments.reason: This is a carved and painted wooden rattle with a double-headed bird form, containing pebbles, made and used by the Tlingit as a ceremonial/shamanic instrument.

instruments.name: Lute
instruments.title: Lute
instruments.reason: The image shows a wooden lute-form instrument attributed to the Yakutat Tlingit, made of wood with sinew and paint, matching the claimed ethnicity and category.

instruments.name: skramla, skallra, rattle
instruments.title: skramla, skallra, rattle
instruments.reason: This is a carved wooden raven rattle with reclining human figures on its back and painted formline-style ornament — a classic Northwest Coast shaman's/ceremonial rattle type strongly associated with the Tlingit and their neighbours.

masks-ritual.name: Mask
masks-ritual.title: Mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden face mask with copper overlay on brows and mouth, and rows of small figures crowning the head — a classic Northwest Coast ceremonial mask form consistent with Tlingit ritual/shamanic practice.

masks-ritual.name: Puppet
masks-ritual.title: Transformation Puppet
masks-ritual.reason: This is a carved bone/ivory articulated figure with shell inlay described as a Tlingit transformation puppet, a type of ritual/shamanic object used by Northwest Coast peoples including the Tlingit; it fits a ceremonial-use object made by the claimed group.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: The image shows a carved wooden beaver mask with painted features, fur detailing and skin straps, consistent with Tlingit ceremonial mask-making traditions of the Pacific Northwest Coast.

masks-ritual.name: mask; religious/ritual equipment
masks-ritual.title: mask; religious/ritual equipment
masks-ritual.reason: This is a carved and painted wooden face mask attributed to a Tlingit medicine shaman, consistent with Northwest Coast ceremonial mask-making traditions used in ritual and healing practice.

masks-ritual.name: Mask
masks-ritual.title: Mask
masks-ritual.reason: The image shows a carved and painted wood ceremonial mask with tusks/teeth, consistent with Tlingit ceremonial mask traditions from the Northwest Coast.

masks-ritual.name: Mask
masks-ritual.title: Mosquito Mask
masks-ritual.reason: This is a carved wooden mosquito/bird-form mask with copper, shell inlay and hide, consistent with Tlingit ceremonial mask-making traditions of the Northwest Coast.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: The image shows a carved wooden face mask painted in blue, red and black with stylized features, described as from Sitka and typical of Tlingit style — a ritual object made and used by the Tlingit.

sculpture.name: Totem pole model
sculpture.title: Totem Pole Model
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden model totem pole with stacked crest figures (faces, animals) in the characteristic Northwest Coast style associated with the Tlingit; this is a well-established Tlingit art form.

arms.name: Knife
arms.title: Knife
arms.reason: This is a Tlingit-style dagger with a carved wooden animal-head handle inlaid with abalone shell, wrapped grip, and metal blade — a well-known Northwest Coast Tlingit weapon form.

garment.name: robe; cloak
garment.title: robe; cloak
garment.reason: This is a Raven's Tail robe, a fringed goat-wool cloak with a geometric diamond weave characteristic of Northwest Coast Tlingit weaving traditions, matching the claimed ethnicity and the museum's attribution.

garment.name: dräkt, mantel, chilkatmantel, garb, costume, garment
garment.title: dräkt, mantel, chilkatmantel, garb, costume, garment
garment.reason: This is a classic Chilkat blanket/robe with the characteristic curvilinear formline totemic design, mountain-goat wool weave, and long twisted fringe, matching the described chief's garment; the museum notes that such robes were made by Chilkat Tlingit (and also Tsimshian), so attribution to Tlingit is well supported.

garment.name: hat
garment.title: hat
garment.reason: This is a woven spruce-root/bark hat with painted Northwest Coast formline crest imagery, a classic Tlingit ceremonial hat type, matching the museum's Tlingit attribution.

metalwork.name: plate
metalwork.title: plate
metalwork.reason: The image shows two Northwest Coast copper shields ("coppers"), a well-known traditional prestige/currency object used by Tlingit and neighboring Northwest Coast peoples; the museum record misclassifies them as ceramic, but they clearly belong to this cultural material category as metalwork, not pottery.
